text:
emily_acme: Hey folks — during a scheduled load test our tenant showed 429s and the dashboard went to 0 credits for ~30s. Response body from the API: {"error":"quota_exhausted", "reset_at":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"}. Billing UI says monthly refill at midnight PST. We're seeing this spike erase credits earlier than expected, any quick checks?

samir: Sorry to hear that — can you paste the tenant id + one example request-id/header? Also which SDK and retry config are you using?

emily_acme: tenant: acme-prod-42
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-***' -H 'x-request-id: 01H7X9ZK' -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
Date: Sun, 01 Mar 2026 00:00:02 GMT
{"error":"quota_exhausted","reset_at":"2026-03-01T00:00:00Z"}

support-bot: [automated] Tenant acme-prod-42: quota_exhausted event at 2026-03-01T00:00:02Z (burst_count=1200).

maria: Quick thought: are you doing aggressive immediate retries on transient errors? Rapid retries + reconnect storm can double-count tokens in some edge cases (stream reconnects especially).

emily_acme: We're using our in-house wrapper around the JS SDK. Retry config was exponential but we tightened it for the test to 100ms base backoff + no jitter to hit sustained throughput. We also had ~200 short reconnects during the test window.

ake_sre: I'm looking at quota-service and metering. Two things to check quickly: 1) whether the client produced a lot of short-lived streaming sessions (reconnects count as new token draws), and 2) whether the tenant's recharge event actually hit the quota cache. If the billing writer finishes but cache invalidation lags, consumers can see 0 until cache TTL refresh.

samir: Can you run this and paste the last 5 lines: rbx audit-events --tenant acme-prod-42 --limit 5 --filter quota_recharge

emily_acme: paste output: 
[2026-03-01T00:00:00Z] quota_recharge succeeded amount=500000
[2026-03-01T00:00:00Z] billing_commit id=bc_9F3
[2026-03-01T00:00:01Z] quota_observed tenant=acme-prod-42 usage_draw=1200
[2026-03-01T00:00:02Z] quota_exhausted
[2026-03-01T00:00:03Z] quota_cache_miss key=tenant:acme-prod-42

maria: That cache_miss is interesting — it suggests the recharge landed in the DB but the in-memory quota cache wasn't refreshed before heavy traffic resumed. With tight immediate retries you'll observe a short window of apparent zero even though persistence shows the new bucket.

ake_sre: Confirmed in internal logs: recharge write committed at 2026-03-01T00:00:00Z but cache invalidation callback delayed ~2.1s due to a memcached GC on that host during the job. During that delay the metering layer returned 0 and rapid retries consumed visible burst simultaneously causing the 429s for a few seconds.

emily_acme: OK that matches what we saw — a 2–3s gap then everything came back. Any recommended immediate workarounds while you fix the cache race?

samir: Short-term options: 1) add randomized jitter to retries (avoid tight 100ms fixed), 2) increase retry base backoff for load tests, or 3) if you need headroom for an exercise, request a service top-up from support (we can add temporary burst credits).

ake_sre: We're rolling a hotfix to ensure the recharge path invalidates cache synchronously for the next deploy and adding a short grace-window in the metering layer to avoid returning 0 if a recent recharge was observed within the last 5s. Patch will go to prod in ~45m.

maria: ETA 45m for hotfix, and I'll follow up here once deployed. For now, recommend applying jitter and slightly longer backoff for your load harness.

emily_acme: Thanks — we'll pause the aggressive test and re-run with jitter. Please post here when the hotfix lands. :thumbsup:

support-bot: [automated] Incident note created: INC-2026-03-01-qa-cache-race. Assigned: ake_sre.

maria: Hotfix deployed to prod at 2026-03-01T00:44:27Z, added synchronous invalidation + 5s grace window. akesre will validate metrics and confirm end state shortly.

ake_sre: Validation: observed no quota_exhausted events for acme-prod-42 during a small repro run after the patch. I'll monitor for 1h and escalate if anything else crops up.

emily_acme: Verified on our side — stable and no 429s after retries with jitter. Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround!"
